items.title: Lords asks government to think again on Cyber Security Bill (AISI powers review agreed 202-155; frontier-AI incident-reporting amendment defeated)
items.excerpt: At report stage on 26 October the House of Lords defeated the government 202-155 to write into the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill a review that must consider giving the AI Security Institute powers; a separate amendment requiring frontier AI developers to report incidents was defeated 95-165, while a government amendment lets ministers take powers where an AI agent loses oversight or control of a regulated network.
items.rationale: Primary parliamentary record of a recorded vote. The Lords wrote an AISI-powers review into the bill and rejected mandatory frontier-AI incident reporting, and ministers gained powers over AI agents that lose control of networks.

items.title: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
items.excerpt: A Delaware corporate-law proposal would allow AI agents to run entire companies with no human at the helm; US Rep. Comer warns owners of AI-run firms could evade liability for 'reckless' AI.
items.rationale: A new corporate-law proposal in the state where most US companies incorporate would let AI agents run firms. Liability concerns are attributed to Rep. Comer. This bears directly on anyone building agentic systems.

items.title: INEC Probes Suspected AI-Generated Photos In Voters' Register
items.excerpt: Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission said in a statement it is investigating suspected AI-generated photographs found in the preliminary Register of Voters published online on October 26, reviewing records for technical or procedural lapses before the final register is certified on December 15, 2026.
items.rationale: Elections axis: a national electoral body formally opened a probe into synthetic photos in its voter register. This is an official action outside the US/EU and a new kind of AI election-integrity issue.

items.title: The U.S.-Taiwan ART's Export Control Puzzle
items.excerpt: Analysis of what the export-control 'alignment' clause in the US-Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade requires of Taipei for advanced chips and AI hardware.
items.rationale: Geopolitics axis: an on-list legal analysis of the trade agreement's export-control alignment clause for AI chips and hardware. The ART clause itself has not been carried before.

items.title: 정부, AI 청소년 보호 강화…심의·법제 정비 본격화
items.excerpt: Korea's Broadcasting, Media and Communications Commission is preparing a standalone 'AI Service User Protection Act' (provisional name) and moving to amend the Network Act and AI Basic Act as AI chatbots' harmful content and youth over-use draw scrutiny.
items.rationale: Korea's media regulator is drafting a standalone AI user-protection law and amendments to the AI Basic Act aimed at chatbot harms to minors. This regional regulation is distinct from the US state lawsuits already published.
